assetCapital.asset: Prime polymer yield and grade transition scrap reduction
assetCapital.basis: 0.12% of polymer throughput recovered from grade transition scrap downgrades and additive giveaway through dynamic non-linear kinetic trajectory optimization
assetCapital.source: ~3.0 MMTPA (~3,000,000 tonnes/year) of polyolefin production (PP, LLDPE, HDPE) across ~9 polymerization and compounding trains at integrated petrochemical complexes. During grade transitions, reactors generate transitional off-spec or wide-spec resin (typically 1.5-3.0% of annual production across 150-200 grade switches/year) that is downgraded to scrap or near-prime utility resin at a ₹20,000-₹30,000/tonne discount against prime resin (~₹100,000-₹115,000/tonne). Dynamic multi-variable trajectory optimization (Agent 2) and gravimetric additive giveaway elimination (Agent 5) conservatively recover 0.12% of throughput value (recovering ~3,600 tonnes/yr from downgrade, or ~18-24 tonnes per transition event). ₹25,000/tonne reflects the net price differential between prime polymer and off-spec transition scrap.

assetRisk.scenario: Fluidized-bed reactor wall sheeting or agglomeration chunking shutdown
assetRisk.source: 9 world-scale polymerization reactor trains across integrated petrochemical complexes. Frequency (0.25/yr) reflects one major wall sheeting or bed chunking event every 4 reactor-years per train (~2.25 events/year across the estate), requiring emergency reactor depressuring, hydrocarbon evacuation, and manual confined-space de-chunking. Consequence (₹20 Cr / ~US$2.4M) reflects 7-10 days of forced outage on a ~350-500 KTA line (~8,000 MT lost production margin at ₹15,000/MT = ₹12 Cr), flared/dumped reaction bed inventory and startup off-spec scrap (~₹4 Cr), plus hydro-blasting mechanical cleanout and distributor grid remediation (~₹4 Cr). Alpha (0.35) reflects the causal share attributable to information and surveillance defects (electrostatic charge accumulation, sticky-point boundary violations in condensed mode, and delayed response to wall skin thermocouple cold-bands); beta (0.35) reflects the 7-agent squad's efficacy in real-time acoustic/thermal precursor detection and anti-static agent dosing optimization (alpha*beta = 0.1225, well within the <=0.18 limit).

rationale: P52 Polymer Process Engineer governs reaction kinetics, catalyst productivity, non-linear grade transition trajectories, fluidized-bed hydrodynamics, compounding extrusion specific mechanical energy, and masterbatch additive formulation across the petrochemical polymer manufacturing footprint. At a scale proxy of ~80 MMTPA refining capacity across 10-11 refineries, downstream petrochemical integration encompasses ~3.0 MMTPA of polyolefin production (PP, LLDPE, HDPE) across ~9 world-scale polymerization and compounding trains located at 3-4 major petrochemical complexes. Sizing at 50 seats represents ~0.16% of total enterprise headcount (~31,000 staff) and ~0.65% of the estate technical population in value_model.js: ~38 plant-based process engineers across 9 continuous trains (~4 per train managing catalyst kinetics, transitions, compounding extrusion, and daily technical services across shifts and day-support), ~6 plant technical services and QA/analytical correlation specialists, and ~6 central petrochemical technical services / Center of Excellence / product application development engineers. Asset Capital is volume-form, capturing 0.12% throughput recovery (~₹9.0 Cr/yr) on 3,000,000 tonnes/year of polymer production at a ₹25,000/tonne downgrade margin differential; dynamic trajectory optimization and gravimetric feeder reconciliation save ~3,600 tonnes/year from being downgraded into off-spec scrap across ~150-200 annual grade transitions, completely distinct from P16 (crude/steam cracker yield), P17 (commercial planning), P28 (fuel blend giveaway), and P46 (APC constraint margin). Asset Risk models avoided catastrophic fluidized-bed wall sheeting or agglomeration chunking shutdowns across 9 reactor trains (0.25 events/train-year, ₹20 Cr consequence, alpha 0.35, beta 0.35, avoiding ₹5.51 Cr/yr in expected losses with alpha*beta held to 0.1225, well below the 0.18 portfolio ceiling). Resource Recovery is strictly null as polymer engineering operates downstream of production and does not influence subsurface reserves, satisfying the portfolio rule prohibiting joint Integrity and Recovery claims.
caveats: 1. If an operator prefers time-form asset capital over volume-form scrap recovery, the equivalent defensible parameterization is: {form: 'time', asset: 'Polymerization reactor trains, via grade transition time compression', units: 9, unitLabel: 'polymerization reactor trains', hoursPerYear: 8760, share: 0.002, ratePerHour: 600000, basis: '0.20% of calendar hours recovered by compressing transition trajectories and de-choking finishing lines (~17.5 h/train/yr)', source: '9 trains; ₹6.0 L/train-hour reflects gross margin contribution of a ~350-400 KTA polyolefin line; delivers ~₹9.46 Cr/yr'}. Volume form is recommended as it directly tracks the petrochemical industry's standard operational KPI: prime polymer yield and transition off-spec tonnage. 2. Failure consequence in assetRisk assumes localized wall sheeting or defluidization chunking requiring manual vessel entry and hydro-blasting cleanout; it deliberately excludes catastrophic reactor runaway exotherms or vessel rupture, which are governed under statutory Process Safety Management (PSM) and emergency depressuring protocols (A12). 3. Operational boundary strictly demarcates against P03 (Board Operator executes DCS setpoints), P16 (Petrochemical Process Engineer handles upstream olefins cracker furnaces), P17 (Production Planner manages commercial supply campaigns), and P46 (Process Control Engineer tunes base APC multivariable controllers).
